children: The Trump administration has told France and Germany to draw down emergency diesel stockpiles to ease global fuel prices or face a potential U.S. diesel export ban, Reuters reported Thursday.
The European Commission, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, and the U.K. will hold a call ⁠to discuss the possible need to release diesel stocks, a European Union official reportedly told Reuters.

U.S. officials have been particularly frustrated with France and Germany, according to the report, believing those countries have not fully followed through on ​earlier commitments to release emergency oil and petroleum stocks to help boost the supply of refined products and lower costs for consumers.

"We've lost some diesel exports from the Middle East, although we're restoring those, and we've lost diesel exports from China, so that's a lot of interruptions," U.S. Energy Secretary Chris ‌Wright told ⁠reporters on Wednesday.
Europe has become increasingly dependent on U.S. fuel after banning ⁠Russian imports ​over Russia's invasion of Ukraine and after the Iran war disrupted supplies from the Middle East.

President Trump said on Wednesday that he has conversations about banning ‌diesel exports "every day" while acknowledging such a ban would "have a negative impact on ​gasoline" prices even while lowering diesel costs.

Crude oil futures rose Thursday following a Reuters report that Chinese refiners have suspended oil product exports for October in an effort to ​preserve domestic inventories, further squeezing war-constrained fuel markets.

China started a week-long holiday on Thursday without giving major refiners a green light to export fuel products to regions other than Hong Kong and Macau in October, and it is not clear whether ​the government would approve refiners' exports after the holiday ends October 7, the report said.
